_schema.applies_to: matcher on {models, periods, results}; null = any. models: endogenous_pension_exogenous_labour (Table 2), endogenous_labour_no_pension (Table 3); periods: claim periods (financial-year end years); results: certified
_schema.variants: the certified variants (data/uk/replay_variants.json) or certified pairs (data/uk/certified_pairs.json) on which a note resting on the engine or a run was checked; it attaches only to those pairs' results. A note resting on the report alone names none and applies to every run
_schema.status: the comparison status this annotation sets, where it sets one; at most one status-setting annotation matches a result
_schema.basis: traceability: raw/pages_layout.txt (PDF page), engine files at the certified pin, or the measured artifact results/uk/childcare_100k/<variant>.json

annotations.text: CBP's figures are net fiscal impacts after a behavioural response: parents choose pension contributions with labour income fixed (Table 2), or choose labour supply with no pension (Table 3), and bunch at £100,000 only when that gains them more than a £1,000 friction. PolicyEngine's counterpart is a static cost (the engine's labour-supply elasticities are zero at the pin), so the two measure different things. CBP publishes no static leg.
annotations.basis: raw/pages_layout.txt PDF page 7 (section 1.3.4, the bunching rule with a £1k friction), PDF page 8 (section 1.3.7, Table 2 and note), PDF page 9 (section 1.4.5, the same rule) and PDF page 10 (section 1.4.6, Table 3 and note); policyengine_uk 2.89.2 variables/input/employment_income.py (adds employment_income_behavioral_response) and variables/gov/simulation/labour_supply_response/employment_income_behavioral_response.py (returns 0 when income_elasticity and substitution_elasticity are both 0); parameters/gov/simulation/labour_supply_responses/income_elasticity.yaml and substitution_elasticity.yaml (0 from 2020-01-01), which no world's reform_dict sets; policyengine_uk 2.132.6, the same files and values, with Simulation.apply_dynamics called only in policyengine_uk/tests; results/uk/childcare_100k/<variant>.json behavioural_response 'none (static)' and gov_tax, which moves by under £1m in every world and year (checked at ingest)

annotations.text: CBP's subsidy includes Tax-Free Childcare: its tables assume £500 of Tax-Free Childcare per child (the model description says up to £2,000). The PolicyEngine counterpart therefore removes both £100,000 limits and adds Tax-Free Childcare to the three free-hours entitlements. Both are counted for England only, as CBP's children are England's births: the engine applies Tax-Free Childcare across the UK, and the change outside England is stated on each result and left out.
annotations.basis: raw/pages_layout.txt PDF page 4 (section 1.2.1: 'the forecast number of births for England'), PDF page 5 (section 1.2.3: 'Up to £2000 is then added to the subsidy to simulate the effect of Tax Free Childcare') and PDF pages 8 and 10 (table notes: '£500 utilisation of TFC'); results/uk/childcare_100k/<variant>.json worlds.free_hours_and_tfc sums_gbp and sums_gbp_england; the pe-england-only construction note

annotations.text: CBP assumes every eligible family uses the full working-parent hours, and gives every child two parents and no siblings. PolicyEngine runs the dataset's own families, values the extended hours at each family's weekly usage input (maximum_extended_childcare_hours_usage), and pays each offer only where the family's take-up input is true. Each result states the usage and take-up the run read and whether the dataset or the engine default supplied them.
annotations.basis: raw/pages_layout.txt PDF page 5 (section 1.2.2: 'every child has two parents and no siblings') and PDF pages 8 and 10 (table notes: 'full utilisation of FCWP'); policyengine_uk 2.89.2 variables/gov/dfe/extended_childcare_entitlement/extended_childcare_entitlement.py (min_ with maximum_extended_childcare_hours_usage), the eligibility variables' defined_for (would_claim_extended_childcare, would_claim_universal_childcare, would_claim_targeted_childcare, would_claim_tfc; each defaults to true); results/uk/childcare_100k/<variant>.json worlds.baseline.dataset_inputs and years.*.take_up and hours_usage

annotations.text: CBP assumes every eligible family uses the full working-parent hours, and gives every child two parents and no siblings. PolicyEngine runs the dataset's own families. It values a child's working-parent hours at the smaller of the child's own weekly usage input (max_free_entitlement_hours_used) and the family's (maximum_extended_childcare_hours_usage), and the universal and targeted hours at the child's own. It pays the working-parent hours only where the family's extended take-up input is true. Each result states the usage and take-up inputs the run read, and whether the dataset or the engine default supplied them.
annotations.basis: raw/pages_layout.txt PDF page 5 (section 1.2.2: 'every child has two parents and no siblings') and PDF pages 8 and 10 (table notes: 'full utilisation of FCWP'); policyengine_uk 2.132.6 variables/gov/dfe/extended_childcare_entitlement/extended_childcare_entitlement_total_per_child.py (min_ of the child's and the family's hours), extended_childcare_entitlement_eligible.py (defined_for would_claim_extended_childcare), universal_childcare_entitlement/universal_childcare_entitlement.py and targeted_childcare_entitlement/targeted_childcare_entitlement.py (the child's hours only), max_free_entitlement_hours_used.py and maximum_extended_childcare_hours_usage.py (default 30), and the take-up inputs would_claim_extended_childcare, would_claim_universal_childcare, would_claim_targeted_childcare, would_claim_tfc; results/uk/childcare_100k/<variant>.json worlds.baseline.dataset_inputs and years.*.take_up and hours_usage

annotations.text: CBP's population is synthetic: children from ONS births for England, each given two parents whose incomes are drawn from the 2022-23 Survey of Personal Incomes (ages 25 to 44). CenTax's Appendix D says the two estimates differ principally because CenTax observes in administrative data what the synthetic model had to assume, and names the treatment of frictions as the most consequential assumption.
annotations.basis: raw/pages_layout.txt PDF pages 4-5 (sections 1.2.1-1.2.2); sources/centax-childcare-100k/raw/pages_layout.txt PDF pages 100-101 (printed pages 99-100, Appendix D)

annotations.text: The appendix gives no sign rule for its tables, and its values are carried as printed. CenTax reads them as revenue raised. PolicyEngine's value is negative for a cost to the Exchequer.
annotations.basis: raw/pages_layout.txt PDF pages 8 and 10 (titles and notes state no sign rule); sources/centax-childcare-100k/raw/pages_layout.txt PDF page 100 (printed page 99: 'CBP estimate that abolishing the threshold would raise between £130 million and £425 million in 2030')

annotations.text: CenTax quotes this cell as £425 million for 2030; the appendix prints 0.427 (£427 million) for 2029/30.
annotations.basis: raw/pages_layout.txt PDF page 10 (Table 3, Abolish Cliff, 2029/30); sources/centax-childcare-100k/raw/pages_layout.txt PDF page 100 (printed page 99, Appendix D)

annotations.text: CBP's columns are financial years (2026/27 is 2026-27). PolicyEngine's annual period 2026 runs the 2026-27 rules: policyengine-uk sets each childcare parameter for year Y to its value on 30 April of Y.
annotations.basis: raw/pages_layout.txt PDF pages 8 and 10 (column labels); policyengine_uk 2.89.2 utils/parameters.py convert_to_fiscal_year_parameters, called in tax_benefit_system.py process_parameters; policyengine_uk 2.132.6 utils/parameters.py convert_to_fiscal_year_parameters, which samples 30 April except for parameters flagged preserve_calendar_dates or fiscal_year_blend, and no file under parameters/gov/dfe or parameters/gov/hmrc/tax_free_childcare sets either flag
